$comment: W8.2 mobile resource evidence ledger (#842). Schema, rules and validator: packages/server/src/serve/resource-evidence.ts. Recomputation: tests/quality/mobile-resource-evidence.test.ts. A lane is either measured/derived with a reproducible number, or blocked-external with the exact condition that unblocks it — never absent. Device rows CANNOT be produced in this repo; do not seed them from a developer laptop, and do not delete them to make the ledger look complete.

observations.blockedReason: Battery drain is only observable on physical hardware. The iOS Simulator reports no battery state, and no host-side proxy for it exists — a number derived here would be fabricated, not measured.
observations.unblockCondition: An enrolled iPhone on the nightly mobile lane running a scripted 30-minute foreground session (Photos scroll, one import, one assistant turn) with Xcode Instruments Energy Log attached; record start/end battery percentage and thermal state.
observations.note: Pair with peak-rss-mb from the same session — thermal throttling makes the two numbers only interpretable together.

observations.blockedReason: The jetsam limit that decides whether a photo import survives backgrounding is a device property. A simulator process inherits the host's memory ceiling, so a simulator number cannot predict the eviction this metric exists to predict.
observations.unblockCondition: An enrolled iPhone on the nightly mobile lane importing the 800-asset fixture with Instruments Allocations attached; record peak footprint and whether jetsam fired.
observations.note: The legacy-device row matters more than the current-device one; add a phone-legacy sibling when a second device is enrolled.

observations.blockedReason: Cold start is dominated by device storage latency and dyld work that a simulator running on host NVMe does not reproduce; the simulator number is optimistic by a margin nobody has measured.
observations.unblockCondition: An enrolled iPhone on the nightly mobile lane measuring first-frame time from a cold launch after a reboot, ten runs, reported as p50/p95.
observations.note: Budget owner is the perceived-latency principle in CONSTITUTION.md; this row is the missing measurement behind it on mobile.

observations.blockedReason: Android emulators report a synthetic battery. Doze and App Standby, which are exactly what a local-first background sync has to survive, do not behave the same way off hardware.
observations.unblockCondition: An enrolled Android device (target: a five-year-old mid-range handset, the class this product claims to serve) on the nightly mobile lane, running the same scripted 30-minute session with Batterystats reset before and dumped after.
observations.note: Run once with battery optimisation on and once off; the delta is the number that decides whether background sync is viable.

observations.blockedReason: The low-memory killer threshold is set per device from total RAM; an emulator configured with host memory never reaches it, so an emulator run cannot fail the way a real one does.
observations.unblockCondition: An enrolled Android device on the nightly mobile lane importing the 800-asset fixture with `adb shell dumpsys meminfo` sampled at 1Hz; record PSS peak and any LMK kill in logcat.
observations.note: The host-proxy vault-bytes row bounds the on-disk half of this; nothing here bounds the resident half.

observations.blockedReason: Cold start on the legacy device class is the number the product's claim rests on, and it is governed by eMMC read latency and ART startup work that no emulator on host hardware reproduces.
observations.unblockCondition: An enrolled Android device on the nightly mobile lane measuring `adb shell am start -W` fully-drawn time after a reboot, ten runs, reported as p50/p95.
observations.note: Report alongside the iOS row; a single-platform number invites the wrong conclusion.

vault.db page_count * page_size divided by content-item count, times 1000, over the year-3 seed at parties=200 photos=800 conversations=10 turns=4. This is a TOTAL-over-items ratio, not a marginal cost: at this fixture scale the fixed schema and index footprint dominates, so the number falls as the vault grows. It is a device-relevant proxy because the SQLite layout on a phone is byte-identical to this one, and it is the only half of the storage question measurable without hardware.

Serialized size of the whole replica_change table after seeding, i.e. the payload a first full replica pass moves. It bounds the bytes a phone downloads on first sync; it does NOT model radio wake cost, retry amplification or compression, which need the blocked device lanes.

Bytes of the strict W8.1 support bundle over the same seeded vault. Recorded here because a diagnostics artifact that grows with vault size would be a scalability defect in the thing built to diagnose scalability defects: the bundle carries counts and sizes, never rows, so this number is expected to stay roughly flat as the fixture grows.
